rules.text: Keep links in the content by default.
Link text can be changed, but the URL for a kept link must remain the same.
Link text must clearly describe the destination page both on its own and in sentence context.

Avoid duplicate link wording. Do not repeat the linked phrase in surrounding sentence text or elsewhere in the alert when meaning is preserved. Keep the destination phrase inside the link only (for example: Find out: Get an access code, not Find out how to get an access code: Get an access code). Avoid the phrase "see" before links; use inclusive alternatives such as "refer to" or "visit". When a link is present, prefer a short lead-in (for example: Find out: or Learn more:) plus unique link text, with no repeated wording outside the anchor.
Never use vague link text like "click here", "here", "learn more", or similar.
If possible, place a link at the end of its sentence.

If a link makes up an entire sentence, move it to a new paragraph and precede it with plain text: Learn more: Descriptive link text. This format can also be used when in-sentence placement is awkward.
Only remove links when there is more than one link and a too-many-links issue is identified; keep one primary link.
Do not remove links unless a too-many-links issue is identified and multiple links are present.
Link text must be concise when possible. Remove information already present in the alert or page context; for example, " - Canada.ca" is not needed.
